name: Squeeze-failure fade — ATR-stop failed break (30m)
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM (the squeeze-failure fade at 30m with an ATR-scaled stop so the fade risks a multiple of prevailing range rather than a fixed fraction — a wider bar that reduces the fee-per-trade drag of the 15m version while keeping the same trapped-crowd thesis): a bb_width multi-window floor is a coiled spring; a downside poke that fails and re-enters the band is a false breakdown that trapped the breakdown crowd. 2025 BB backtests confirm naive band-breaks are a coin-flip because false breaks dominate, so we fade them: the trapped shorts' buy-to-cover fuels the snap-back. Entry (long): bb_width below a fitted floor (spring) AND range_position below a fitted floor (poked to the lower band) AND atr above a fitted floor (the poke was a real volatility burst, not a dead tape — this is the distinct third gauge vs the 15m rsi version). The exit uses an ATR-multiple stop so a fresh entry is not knocked out by ordinary noise. The counterparty is the mechanical band-break sellers whose stop cascade is our fuel. Distinct from squeeze-then-trend (buys the confirmed break). Exit: range_position crosses up back into mid-band (snap-back done) or ATR-stop/TP/time. DISCONFIRMER 1: drop the squeeze pre-condition (fade any lower-band poke) — if it works as well, the squeeze is inert and this is generic false-breakout fading, not a vol-family edge. DISCONFIRMER 2: net of ~20bps at 30m the small fades must clear; if per-trade edge < fees the trade count kills it. DISCONFIRMER 3: if the atr-floor leg fires on nearly every squeeze-poke bar it adds no information -> the burst filter is inert.
catalyst: a squeeze whose failed downside break traps shorts on a real volatility burst
